title: Miso and Harissa Spaghetti with Crispy Crumbs
changes_from_base: Carbonara-style: beaten eggs, miso, harissa and Parmesan make a silky sauce in the hot pasta, topped with crunchy parsley crumbs.
summary: A carbonara-style spaghetti made silky with egg, miso, harissa and Parmesan, topped with golden parsley breadcrumbs.

ingredients.item: fine salt for 3 litres of pasta water (0.5%)
ingredients.note: about 2½ tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Crumbs
steps.text: Heat the oil in the small pan over medium-high heat, add the panko, parsley and salt and stir constantly for 2-3 min until golden. Tip into a bowl.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Boil the spaghetti in 3 litres salted water until just short of al dente. Save a mug of the water and drain.

steps.title: Sauce base
steps.text: In the bowl, whisk the miso, harissa and oil with 3 tbsp of the hot pasta water until smooth, then whisk in the eggs.

steps.title: Make it creamy
steps.text: Return the pasta to the pot over the lowest heat, add the egg mixture and Parmesan and stir hard and constantly. Add a few spoonfuls of water and keep stirring 1-2 min until the sauce is thick, glossy and steaming (71 °C). Keep it moving, as constant stirring is what stops the egg scrambling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Take off the heat, taste (miso and cheese are both salty) and serve at once with the crumbs.

tips: Use the lowest heat and never stop stirring once the eggs go in.
Have bowls warm and ready; the sauce thickens as it sits.
Taste before salting, as miso and Parmesan are both salty.
storage: Best eaten straight away; egg sauces do not reheat well. Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
